description.short_caption: Chest radiograph showing bilateral lung fields and mediastinal structures.
description.detailed_description: This is a frontal chest radiograph showing both lung fields, the heart, and mediastinal structures. The lung fields appear clear without obvious consolidation, mass, or pleural effusion. The cardiac silhouette is within normal limits, and the diaphragm is well-defined bilaterally. Bony structures, including the ribs and spine, are visible and appear intact. The trachea is midline.

Case_10004/figure2.jpg.source_caption: CT scan of the chest, lung view.

description.short_caption: Coronal CT scan of the chest showing lung fields and mediastinum.
description.detailed_description: This is a coronal CT scan of the chest, lung window view. The lung fields are visualized with clear delineation of pulmonary structures. There is an area of increased density in the left lower lung field, suggestive of consolidation or mass. The mediastinum appears midline, and no obvious pleural effusion is noted. The bony structures, including the ribs and spine, are also visible.
visible_findings: coronal CT view of the chest
increased density in the left lower lung field

Case_10004/figure3.jpg.source_caption: CT scan of the chest, abdominal view.

description.short_caption: Coronal CT scan of the chest and upper abdomen.
description.detailed_description: This is a coronal CT scan showing the chest and upper abdominal regions. The image highlights the thoracic cavity, including the lungs, mediastinum, and portions of the upper abdominal organs. The bony structures of the spine and ribs are visible. There is no clear evidence of gross abnormalities such as masses, fluid collections, or fractures in this view, but further analysis may be required.
visible_findings: coronal view of thorax and upper abdomen
reveal_triggers: CT scan of chest and abdomen

description.short_caption: Gram stain of cyst aspirate showing mixed bacterial morphology.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a Gram stain of a cyst aspirate. The field contains numerous polymorphonuclear leukocytes (PMNs) and mixed bacterial forms, including Gram-positive cocci and Gram-negative bacilli. The background appears proteinaceous, consistent with an inflammatory exudate. The staining highlights the bacterial morphology and cellular components.

description.short_caption: Gram stain of cyst aspirate showing filamentous branching structures.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a Gram stain of a cyst aspirate. The field contains filamentous, branching structures that are suggestive of bacterial or fungal organisms. The background appears to have cellular debris and inflammatory cells, consistent with an infectious process. The branching structures are stained purple, indicating Gram-positive organisms.

description.short_caption: Histopathology of tissue biopsy with Steiner stain showing dark-staining organisms.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a histopathological section of tissue stained with Steiner stain, which highlights microorganisms in dark brown to black against a lighter background. The central area contains dense, dark-staining structures consistent with clusters of microorganisms. Surrounding tissue appears lighter and shows cellular and extracellular matrix structures. The Steiner stain is commonly used to identify spirochetes and other microorganisms in tissue samples.
visible_findings: dark-staining organisms in the central area
lighter surrounding tissue with cellular structures
contrast between stained organisms and background

Case_10004/figure6.jpg.source_caption: Biopsy of tissue, H and E stain.

description.short_caption: Histopathology of tissue biopsy with H&E stain showing granulomatous inflammation.
description.detailed_description: This histopathology image shows a tissue section stained with hematoxylin and eosin (H&E). The central area contains necrotic material surrounded by a rim of epithelioid histiocytes and scattered multinucleated giant cells, consistent with granulomatous inflammation. Numerous inflammatory cells, including lymphocytes, are visible in the surrounding tissue. The findings suggest a granulomatous process, potentially infectious or non-infectious in etiology.

Case_10004/figure8.jpg.source_caption: Biopsy of excised tissue, Brown-Hopps (gram) stain.

description.short_caption: Brown-Hopps (gram) stain showing filamentous bacteria in tissue biopsy.
description.detailed_description: This is a high-magnification image of a tissue biopsy stained with the Brown-Hopps (gram) stain. The image reveals numerous filamentous, branching bacteria that stain gram-positive (dark purple) against a yellowish background. The surrounding tissue matrix and scattered inflammatory cells are visible. The findings are suggestive of an infection with filamentous bacteria, such as Actinomyces or Nocardia.
